newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Korea refiners maximise crude run on good prices.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea refiners maximise crude run on good prices.

text.p: South Korean refiners are operating their crude distillation units (CDUs) at above design capacity to take advantage of high product prices and good regional demand, industry sources in Seoul said on Monday.
"Based on the export nominations, at least one refiner is operating at above 100%," one industry source said.
South Korean refiners also operated above design capacity in April, ahead of the maintenance season in May and June.
Industry sources said South Korea had sold between eight and 10 spot gas oil cargoes for September lifting, most of them to China or Hong Kong.
The push for gas oil exports comes despite the scheduled shutdown of Ssangyong Oil Refining Co's 200,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) CDU between September 2 and 22.
Part of the increase in exports was due to the startup of Yukong Ltd's new 200,000-bpd CDU in early September. It is expected to start full commercial production by the end of September.

South Korean refiners had already sold out all their September-lifting gas oil cargoes on strong regional demand due to uncertainties following the U.S. missile attacks on Iraq last week, the sources said.
The attacks triggered sudden demand from China and many of South Korea's September gas oil cargoes were snapped up, he added.
One Korean refiner said the last 30,000-tonne cargo for September lifting was sold on Friday at about $27.00 per barrel on a free-on-board (fob) South Korea basis.
"Most of the September cargoes were sold on a fixed price basis as the buyers were not willing to buy on a floating basis," the refiner said.
"This was the highest price that was paid for a September cargo," he added.
